big_case.notes: Challenges Chicago's graduated traffic-enforcement forfeiture scheme (MCC § 9-100-120), under which the City impounds and sells or scraps vehicles of owners with unpaid parking tickets without offsetting the debt or refunding surplus proceeds. The case sits at the doctrinal intersection of Tyler v. Hennepin County (2023) and the police-power forfeiture line under Bennis v. Michigan (1996), affecting municipal fine-collection practices nationwide and drawing two post-Long Conference relists plus a statement respecting the denial of certiorari by Justice Sotomayor joined by Justice Gorsuch. However, the stakes of this specific vehicle were significantly constrained by its exclusively facial Takings Clause posture and record facts showing one plaintiff's car was sold for scrap and the other's relinquished to a lienholder.
